scope: Paired SIMLOX 2017 MaxPMProfile time-varying capacity at one unit: both arms 0 until h24.25 and 1 until h24.75, then rise to 2 versus hold at 1. Observe physical CAL24 PM work around each capacity boundary.

manual.rule: Unit.MAXPMP references MaxPMProfile, whose timed <LIMIT> rows override Unit.MAXPM; noncritical PM is postponed above the current limit and critical PM can bypass the limit. Explicit limit periods must not overlap.

frozen_source_delta: Derive both arms from accepted D13 static MAXPM=2 input with seed1, two aircraft, three scheduled h8/h20/h32 missions, one CAL24 PM with DTIM0.5, and 36-hour horizon.
Set Unit.MAXPM=0 as a scalar fallback and Unit.MAXPMP=CAP24 in both arms. Add one MaxPMProfile with nonoverlapping 0-24.25 limit0, 24.25-24.75 limit1, and 24.75-36 limit2 (rise) or limit1 (hold).
Only ProblemDescription and the final MaxPMProfile.MAXPM cell differ between arms.
acceptance_hypotheses: Both arms create CAL24 PM task objects at h24 and do no physical PM work before the h24.25 capacity increase.

At h24.25 one aircraft physically starts PM in each arm. At h24.75 the rise arm starts the second aircraft while the first is still working; the hold arm waits until capacity is released. Native events and report bins must distinguish this.
Both inputs roundtrip populated cells, have zero converter errors and usable SXOs; report PM occupancy, mission outcomes, and terminal state reconcile.
gate: Publish only if the native logs prove the timed profile's physical PM effect with an otherwise identical paired source, clean conversion, sealed raw evidence, and independent read-only replay. If import or behavior differs, retain the immutable run as an excluded diagnostic; revise a new version. Do not infer hidden capacity counters.
execution_guard: Session-0 SSH with sshd ancestor, Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue, GUI PID 13340/session 1 identity, immutable run path, 60-second targeted child watchdog, source hashes before/after and raw SHA-256 closure.
limits: Two aircraft, one seed, one unit, one CALHOURS PM, one 0-to-1-to-2 profile transition sequence; no general boundary law, overlap-error behavior, nested/repeated profile, GUI or cross-engine claim.
